exposure: Outpatient therapeutic rest in early labor using intramuscular morphine sulfate and promethazine
cohort: Pregnant women presenting for labor evaluation
finding: Outpatient therapeutic rest in early labor did not significantly affect the rate of active labor at admission but was associated with a lower need for labor induction and high patient satisfaction without increasing adverse perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: There was no detectable difference in the primary outcome of active labor at admission between patients who accepted outpatient therapeutic rest and those who declined it; however, fewer participants in the treatment group eventually required induction of labor, and mode of delivery did not differ between groups.
